web.title: RF-LSTM carbon price prediction based on CEEMDAN decomposition and multiscale entropy reconstruction
web.description:
As global climate change intensifies, the establishment of an effective carbon pricing mechanism has become a core policy tool for achieving a low-carbon economic transition. The European Union launched the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) in 2005 to reduce greenhouse gas emissions at the lowest overall cost.^1^ The EU ETS has demonstrated significant influence on global carbon markets by internalizing carbon costs through market mechanisms.^2^ Carbon pricing serves as a financial instrument for addressing environmental externalities and as a crucial link between environmental policy and the economic system.^3^ Its price signals directly influence firms’ technological investment decisions and the trajectory of industrial restructuring^4^. Between 2013 and 2014, China launched seven regional carbon trading pilots in Guangdong, Hubei, Shanghai, Tianjin, Beijing, Chongqing, and Shenzhen^5^. In 2016, the Fujian carbon market was opened, bringing eight operational carbon markets in China^6^. Since its launch, key design parameters such as sector coverage, annual quota reduction rates, and the proportion of free allowances have significantly nonlinear impacts on carbon prices^7^. However, as the market mechanism is still evolving, the interaction between policy adjustments and market expectations has caused the carbon price series to exhibit high volatility, nonlinearity, and multifractal characteristics. Traditional econometric models struggle to capture these complex dynamic features. As a result, forecasting carbon prices remains a major challenge, attracting increasing attention from researchers.

In this study, the predicted step length was set at 5. The step size was set to five because the carbon market operates only on trading days, with no price quotations on weekends and certain public holidays.

web.title: Multi-objective energy scheduling in multiple energy system considering economic and environmental objective functions
web.description: The growing integration of renewable energy sources along with multi-energy technologies has introduced new challenges for the coordinated management of intricate energy systems amid carbon and operational uncertainties. This study presents a multi-objective risk-aware optimization framework with optimizing the operation of multiple energy system. First, a refined carbon-flow modeling technique is developed to depict carbon propagation in the multi-energy networks. An energy-quality-coefficient-based method for carbon-flow allocation is introduced for devices that convert multiple inputs and outputs to monitor the temporal movement of carbon emissions through energy storage systems. Additionally, a theoretical framework for the propagation and amplification of carbon uncertainty is established, revealing that the uncertainty in carbon flow can surpass the corresponding uncertainty in energy flow. The proposed modeling combines economic costs, carbon emissions, and operational risks through a multi-objective optimization model that includes a risk-preference coefficient and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). Numerical results show that the suggested method lowers carbon-emission deviation to 12.34%, in contrast to 45.67% for the deterministic model. Additionally, seasonal scheduling outcomes further highlight its resilience in extreme weather conditions. In scenarios of high-temperature summers and cold-wave winters, the proposed approach cuts average daily operating costs by 13.0% and 15.6%, respectively, while also reducing carbon-emission intensity by 16.6% and 17.2%, and enhancing renewable-energy usage. These findings indicate that the proposed framework effectively balances economic efficiency, carbon reduction, renewable-energy integration, and operational risk, offering a strong strategy for the sustainable operation of complex multi-energy systems amid uncertainty.

web.title: Removal of carbofuran from aqueous solutions using activated carbon derived from Pistacia khinjuk stocks (bıttım) shell waste
web.description:
# Removal of carbofuran from aqueous solutions using activated carbon derived from *Pistacia khinjuk* stocks (bıttım) shell waste
## Abstract
Pesticides are important environmental pollutants that require effective removal to protect ecosystems and human health. This study investigated carbofuran removal from water using KOH-activated carbon derived from *Pistacia khinjuk* Stocks (bıttım) shell waste. The resulting adsorbent exhibited a high specific surface area (1552 m² g⁻¹). Under the selected conditions (50 mg L⁻¹ carbofuran, 0.01 g adsorbent, 0.25 L solution, pH 4.0, 25 min, and 298 K), the highest experimental adsorption capacity was 324.3 mg g⁻¹. In synthetic water, the adsorption capacity was 276.5 mg g⁻¹, retaining approximately 85.3% of that obtained in ultrapure water. The apparent thermodynamic parameters and the decrease in adsorption capacity with increasing temperature were consistent with favorable adsorption and an exothermic temperature dependence under the investigated conditions. The Langmuir isotherm best described the equilibrium data. Adsorption appeared to involve hydrophobic and π–π electron donor–acceptor interactions, while electrostatic attraction likely played a limited role. These findings demonstrate the potential of bıttım shell-derived activated carbon as a biomass-derived adsorbent for carbofuran removal from water.

web.title: Short-duration, managed grazing system increases net ecosystem carbon uptake and water use efficiency on a working ranch
web.description:
Grasslands are globally significant carbon (C) sinks, but data quantifying how multi-paddock, managed grazing sytems alter ecosystem fluxes and the annual C budget are limited. We hypothesized a high-intensity (150 cow-calf pair), short-duration (2 days), rotational grazing system targeting 50% utilization, followed by extended rest and recovery, could improve net C uptake (net ecosystem production; NEP), water use efficiency (WUE), and the net amount of C sequestered (C budget) by the ecosystem annually. We quantified water and C fluxes over two full years using eddy covariance and field-based measurements of C removed by grazers on a U.S. northern prairie working cattle ranch. Managed grazing nearly doubled annual NEP for both yearly cycles, as compared to ungrazed control. The net amount of C sequestered under managed grazing reached 1.01 and 0.37 Mg C ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ in the first and second cycle, respectively—53% and 23% greater than ungrazed control. Grazing initially decreased leaf area index and daily C uptake, but the ecosystem gradually recovered through autumn, with elevated C uptake and resource-use efficiencies. Our findings demonstrate that improvements in grassland C uptake, C sequestration, and allocation of water to production can be achieved through inclusion of grazers and adaptive grassland management.

Biomass was 42% C, so the sum of all C removed by grazers was 0.35 Mg C ha− 1 and 0.54 Mg C ha− 1, respectively, for the first and second annual cycle (Table [1](/articles/s41598-026-72714-5#Tab1)).

Phillips, R.L., Zhou, X. & Bo, H. Short-duration, managed grazing system increases net ecosystem carbon uptake and water use efficiency on a working ranch. *Sci Rep* **16**, 30674 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-72714-5

web.title: Bio-waste-derived chicken feather carbon-integrated ZnGa2O4 nanocomposites for asymmetric supercapacitor application
web.description: The pursuit of next-generation energy storage systems necessitates the development of advanced electrode materials that offer both high charge storage capacity and outstanding cycling stability to meet the increasing need for advanced energy storage devices. Engineering hybrid nanostructures that combine conductivity, porosity, and electrochemical activity offers a promising pathway to elevate supercapacitor performance. This study reports the hydrothermal synthesis of ZnGa2O4/chicken feather carbon (ZGO/CFC) composites using varying amounts of chicken feather-derived carbon (40, 65, and 100 mg) as a sustainable carbon source. Comprehensive characterization techniques including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman Spectroscopy, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analyses confirm the formation of a well-crystallized cubic ZnGa2O4 structure, along with its morphological characteristics, elemental composition, and porosity. Electrochemical characterization reveal that the ZnGa2O4/100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode exhibits the highest specific capacitance of about 642.0 F g− 1 at 1 A g− 1 surpassing its counterparts. Asymmetric supercapacitor fabricated from ZnGa2O4/100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode shows specific capacitance of 67.33 F g− 1 with energy and power densities of about 21.04 Wh kg− 1 ,750 W kg− 1 respectively. In addition, it achieves a capacitive retention rate of about 94.0% and coulombic efficiency of about 95.0% which demands the integration of metal oxides with low-cost, renewable carbon materials as an effective strategy for advancing the performance of supercapacitors. The optimized ZGO/CFC composites demonstrate promising prospects for high-performance supercapacitor applications, facilitating the development for green energy storage solutions.
